- If sentiment is positive (≥0.2) in recent days, model tends to underreact — increase forecast slightly to avoid underestimating upward momentum.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.0) and price is trending down, model often overcorrects — reduce forecast slope to avoid premature bottoming.  
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior day), model frequently overestimates continuation — cap forecast growth to 5–7% max for next 3–5 days.  
- When sentiment shifts from neutral to positive, model often lags — adjust forecast to align with sentiment change within 2–3 days.  
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 80), model tends to overpredict recovery — reduce forecast slope by 10–15% for next 5 days.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates downward drift — add 0.5–1.0% buffer to forecast if sentiment is neutral or negative.
